title: Meeting room domain model
idea: The meeting room domain model separates what exists (Room, Employee), what is planned (Meeting), and what claims a room for an Interval (Booking).

analogy.text: A paper sign-up sheet taped to each room's door. Each line names who booked, when, and for what meeting.
analogy.breaks: A sheet cannot refuse an overlapping line; Calendar does.

points: Room and Employee are records: fixed facts with ids.
Interval is a half-open value object; end must be after start.
A Meeting has an organizer, guests and an Interval; Booking adds a Room.
Each Room has one Calendar of active Bookings, sorted by start time.

edges.label: organized by 1
edges.caption: A Meeting has one organizer. Guests are stored as Employee ids, not objects.

edges.label: has 1
edges.caption: A Meeting owns one Interval. Interval is a value object: equal fields mean equal values.

edges.label: for 1
edges.caption: A Booking is for one Meeting. A meeting with no room yet has no Booking.

edges.label: in 1
edges.caption: A Booking claims exactly one Room. A Room has many Bookings over time.

edges.label: for 1
edges.caption: Each Room has one Calendar. It is the only place that answers isFree.

edges.label: holds 0..*
edges.caption: The Calendar keeps active Bookings keyed by start, so a lookup checks only one neighbour.

edges.label: has
edges.caption: BookingStatus is an enum. The lifecycle page turns it into a state machine.

code.title: The model in Java 17
code.caption: Records for facts and values, a class for Booking because its status changes, and invariants in constructors.

walk.text: Build an Employee, a Room for six, a Calendar, and book a 10:00 meeting.
Ask about a back-to-back slot and an overlapping slot.
Two bad inputs are refused: an empty interval and too many people.
Interval rejects end before or equal to start and owns the overlap rule.
Meeting copies the guest list and counts the organizer in its headcount.
`lowerEntry` returns the latest booking starting before our end; only it can clash.
`add` checks capacity and overlap before storing the Booking.

pitfalls: Do not put a busy flag on Room; a room is busy only for some intervals.
Store guests as ids; embedding Employee objects copies data that later changes.
Count the organizer in headcount, or a full room gets one person too many.

quiz.q: What does the last line of DomainModel print?
options: rejected: start must be before end
quiz.why: Six guests plus the organizer make seven. `checkFits` compares seven with capacity six and throws, and the catch prints it.

takeaway: Rooms exist, meetings are planned, bookings claim a room for an interval.

starters: Why is Interval a record and Booking a class?
Why does lowerEntry find every possible clash?
Should Meeting and Booking be one class in a smaller design?
